strategies.name: Pythagorean Regression (Luck Fade)
strategies.thesis: A team whose actual win% sits far above its Pythagorean win% has been winning close games it did not really dominate; the reverse is true for a team underperforming its scoring profile. Fade the lucky, back the unlucky.
strategies.residualInfo: Pythagorean win% vs actual win% (not used by the originated line).
strategies.where: luckDiff = home.luck - away.luck; adjustment is applied against the luckier team.

lambda.note: Margin points per 1.00 of luck differential.

G3.detail: all inputs are season-to-date or pre-game published reports

G4.detail: single-leg strategy, no intra-leg correlation to control

G5.detail: at least one signal is below its break-even (worst margin -12.37 pp)

G6.detail: BLOCKED: no graded historical bet log exists in this repository

strategies.name: Recent-Form vs Season Divergence
strategies.thesis: When a team's last-10 record disagrees materially with its full-season record, trust the larger sample: fade the hot streak, back the slump.
strategies.residualInfo: Last-10 win% vs season win% (not used by the originated line).

lambda.note: Margin points per 1.00 of L10-vs-season differential.

G3.detail: all inputs are season-to-date or pre-game published reports

strategies.name: Venue-Split Divergence
strategies.thesis: Some teams are materially better or worse at home than their overall net rating implies, and likewise on the road. Compare the home team's home record with the away team's road record.
strategies.residualInfo: Home/away split records (the line uses a league-average home-court term only).
strategies.trigger: |home-team home win% - away-team road win%| >= 0.30, with >= 5 games in each split

lambda.note: Margin points per 1.00 of venue-split differential.

strategies.name: Availability Fade (official injury report)
strategies.thesis: Teams carrying a heavier unavailability load are weaker than their season-to-date net rating implies, because that net rating was earned with healthier rotations.
strategies.residualInfo: Weighted unavailability index built from the official NBA injury report. Explicitly NOT applied to the published line.
strategies.where: rotationDiff = home.rotationIndex - away.rotationIndex. Weights: Out 1.00, Doubtful 0.75, Questionable 0.40, Probable 0.15, Available 0.00. G League two-way and G League assignment rows are EXCLUDED, because those players were not in the NBA rotation. NOT YET SUBMITTED is also excluded - it is an absence of information, not information.

lambda.note: Margin points per 1.00 of unavailability index. UNCALIBRATED.

strategies.name: Emirates NBA Cup point-differential incentive
strategies.thesis: If the Cup group tiebreaker is point differential, teams have a documented incentive to keep scoring late in blowouts, biasing Cup games toward the over.
strategies.residualInfo: Whether a game is an Emirates NBA Cup group game (known from the official schedule).
strategies.trigger: game is an Emirates NBA Cup group game
strategies.where: Applied to the projected total only.

lambda.note: Points added to the projected total for a Cup group game.

strategies.name: Extreme-Streak Mean Reversion
strategies.thesis: Very long losing (or winning) streaks are partly noise. Fade streaks of 6+ games in either direction.
strategies.residualInfo: Current win/loss streak length (not used by the originated line).
strategies.trigger: either team on a streak of 6+ games
strategies.where: signedStreak = +n for a W n streak, -n for an L n streak; adjustment favours the team on the longer losing streak.

lambda.note: Margin points per game of streak beyond 5, applied in the mean-reverting direction.

strategies.name: Totals: Fade the Extremes
strategies.thesis: Projected totals at the extremes of the distribution regress: the highest-projected games tend to land lower than the raw scoring-environment maths implies, and the lowest higher.
strategies.residualInfo: Distance of the originated total from the league norm (the line itself, regressed back).
strategies.where: totalVsNorm = projected total - 2 x league-average PPG.

lambda.note: Fraction of the league-norm gap removed from the projected total.

strategies.name: Cross-Game Parlay Builder (correlation-controlled)
strategies.thesis: Parlaying legs from different games keeps inter-leg correlation at ~0, so the fair parlay price is the product of the leg prices. Parlays then amplify per-leg edge multiplicatively - and amplify vig just as fast when there is no edge.
strategies.residualInfo: Independence across games (verified by construction, since games are disjoint).
strategies.trigger: at least 2 qualifying legs, each from a different game

G3.detail: all inputs are season-to-date or pre-game published reports

strategies.name: Same-Game Parlay: correlation mispricing
strategies.thesis: Books price same-game parlays by multiplying leg probabilities as if the legs were independent. When two legs from one game are POSITIVELY correlated, the true joint probability is higher than the product, so the independent price is generous. When they are NEGATIVELY correlated the independent price is a trap.
strategies.residualInfo: Within-game correlation between market outcomes, measured by Monte-Carlo (not used anywhere else).
inputs: simulated joint distribution of margin and total

wl.method: W-L from T2 (S04) compared with W-L from T1 (S02) for every team appearing in the Nov 13-15 slate, which is all 30 teams.

ppgIdentity.check: mean(PPG) across all 30 teams must equal mean(OPP PPG), because every point scored is a point allowed

fairLineSanity.check: Monte-Carlo P(home covers its own originated spread) must be ~0.500, otherwise the line and the simulator disagree
